:::{#def-cross-product-matrix}
#### Cross-product matrix

Let $\matr{A}$ be an $m \times n$ matrix with columns $\vecf{a}_1, \ldots, \vecf{a}_n$
and $\matr{B}$ an $m \times q$ matrix with columns $\vecf{b}_1, \ldots, \vecf{b}_q$.
The **cross-product matrix** of $\matr{A}$ and $\matr{B}$
is the $n \times q$ matrix $\tprod{\matr{A}}{\matr{B}}$,
whose entry $(i, j)$ is the dot product $\vecf{a}_i \cdot \vecf{b}_j$.

:::

::: notes
Each entry pairs a column of $\matr{A}$ with a column of $\matr{B}$, so we can call it a column-column [product](linear-algebra.qmd#def-matrix-mult).
Ordinary [matrix multiplication](linear-algebra.qmd#def-matrix-mult) instead pairs a row of the left factor with a column of the right factor, a row-by-column product [@northwestern_linalg_chap1, Section 2].

This is what R's `crossprod(A, B)` computes, and `crossprod(A)` is $\tprod{\matr{A}}{\matr{A}}$.
In NumPy it has no name of its own: write `A.T @ B`.

For two column vectors it is the $1 \times 1$ matrix holding their [dot product](linear-algebra.qmd#def-dot-product).
It is unrelated to the cross product $\vecf{u} \times \vecf{v}$ of two vectors in $\reals^3$,
and differs from the Frobenius inner product $\operatorname{tr}\paren{\tprod{\matr{A}}{\matr{B}}}$,
which sums the diagonal of this matrix into a single number.
:::
